summary: No region-specific trans law, ordinance, incident series or enforcement finding was located for this division - the research dossier lists it among the units with no sub-national signal, so the national evidence applies: the congressional Women and Family Committee approved bills banning trans people from public restrooms in early 2025 (floor vote pending), and the national university observatory recorded 54 LGBTI homicides and 170 rights violations in 2020-2023, more than half of the homicide victims trans women (30 of 54). The absence of local findings reflects Peru's lack of hate-crime statistics rather than any positive local difference.

sources.summary: Infobae Peru (20 Feb 2025): the congressional Women and Family Committee unanimously approved bills (from Montoya and Muñante) banning trans people from public restrooms, with exceptions for custody, medical need, and accompanying children under 12 or elderly/disabled persons, plus a ban on ambiguous bathroom signage; a floor vote is pending. Recounts the July 2023 complaint over 'feminine/masculine identity' bathroom labels at Jorge Chávez airport and LGTBIQ activist Gianna Camacho's objection that the measures weaponise stigma against trans people.

IDEHPUCP human-rights bulletin (15 April 2025): legal analysis of Congress's proposed prohibition of trans people from public restrooms, based on bills 6505/2023-CR and 8457/2023-CR fused at the Women and Family Committee; contextualises it alongside the 2 April 2025 Plenary approval (exempted from a second vote) of the children's sexual-indemnity law, framing the package as legalised discrimination against trans access to public space.

Agencia Presentes (22 July 2024): the Cayetano Heredia University LGBTI Rights Observatory's annual report recorded 54 LGBTI homicides and 170 rights violations in 2020-2023 - more than half the homicide victims were trans women (30 of 54), with 19 killings in 2023 (12 trans women); documents torture-level violence, and a February 2023 case in which the 'Los Gallegos' gang extorted sex workers ('cupos') in central Lima before murdering Rubí Torres Silvano (31) in Carabayllo. Peru has no hate-crime law, so regional comparisons cannot come from official statistics.
